proposals.evidence: Full CDIAL distinguishes masculine trayaḥ/trāyaḥ from neuter trīṇi. The Bhil survey ṭiṇ has the i vowel and final nasal of section 3, alongside Prakrit tiṇṇi, Gujarati traṇ and Marathi/Hindi tīn; it cannot be assigned to the a-vowel sections from the English numeral alone. Source retroflex onset and final ṇ are retained. The family link does not select a particular modern donor.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL karṇa gives Prakrit kaṇṇa and Gujarati/Marathi/Hindi kān “ear”, with widespread nasal place variants across its reflexes. The selected neighbouring Bhil attestations retain the same kā- plus nasal body-part stem; their word-final ŋ is explicitly present in the original survey transcription, not silently normalized to n. This is a family assignment; the phonetic value/place of the final nasal remains as transcribed.
